summary: Ravalli County, MT platform on the Bitterroot NF: a tent cabin and firefinder platform dated 1937, abandoned 1940; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says abandoned in 1940, and the FFLA Montana list says abandoned, not gone. No source says what stands today.

events.note: Firelookout.com dates a tent cabin and firefinder platform to 1937

evidence.supports: tent cabin and firefinder platform dated 1937; abandoned 1940
the Osborne Fire Finder is an alidade that lookouts used to find a bearing to smoke
evidence.quote: The Osborne Fire Finder is a type of alidade used by fire lookouts to find a directional bearing

evidence.supports: the bearing to smoke was used to alert fire crews to a wildland fire
evidence.quote: to smoke in order to alert fire crews to a wildland fire

evidence.supports: FFLA list shows the site as abandoned

association list gives the structure type as a platform at 46.3675 north, 113.85715 west

corrections.why: The FFLA Montana list shows Owen Point as Platform Abandoned, not Gone, and firelookout.com says Abandoned 1940 with nothing about a structure remaining. Abandoned is not in the status vocabulary, so unknown is the nearest fit; an editor may want an abandoned status.

notes_for_editor: Record status gone is contradicted by both listings (see corrections); county, agency, kind platform and coordinates match the FFLA list. Firelookout.com gives only the 1937 entry and the 1940 abandonment; staffing, fires, the structure's condition and access are not described anywhere, so they are left out. The firefinder definition comes from the Wikipedia article on the Osborne Fire Finder, a specific model; the story now says a firefinder, such as the Osborne Fire Finder, lets lookouts sight the bearing of smoke, and does not call every firefinder an alidade (the article's earlier Ronalds fire finder was a theodolite on a watchtower). The Forest Lookouts page (source 4) gives the legal location 7N-18W-9 and adds nothing else. Two searches; four reads (firelookout, Forest Lookouts, FFLA list, Wikipedia). No photo URL found.
